In [[mathematics]], the '''Arakawa–Kaneko zeta function''' is a generalisation of the [[Riemann zeta function]] which generates special values of the [[polylogarithm]] function.

==Definition==
The zeta function <math>\xi_k(s)</math> is defined by

:<math>\xi_k(s) = \frac{1}{\Gamma(s)} \int_0^{+\infty} \frac{t^{s-1}}{e^t-1}\mathrm{Li}_k(1-e^{-t}) \, dt \ </math>

where Li<sub>''k''</sub> is the ''k''-th polylogarithm 

:<math>\mathrm{Li}_k(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{z^n}{n^k} \ . </math>

==Properties==
The integral converges for <math>\Re(s) > 0</math> and <math>\xi_k(s)</math> has [[analytic continuation]] to the whole complex plane as an [[entire function]].

The special case ''k''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 gives <math>\xi_1(s) = s \zeta(s+1)</math> where <math>\zeta</math> is the [[Riemann zeta-function]].

The special case ''s''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 remarkably also gives <math>\xi_k(1) = \zeta(k+1)</math> where <math>\zeta</math> is the [[Riemann zeta-function]].

The values at integers are related to [[multiple zeta function]] values by

:<math>\xi_k(m) = \zeta_m^*(k,1,\ldots,1) </math>

where

:<math>\zeta_n^*(k_1,\dots,k_{n-1},k_n)=\sum_{0<m_1<m_2<\cdots<m_n}\frac{1}{m_1^{k_1}\cdots m_{n-1}^{k_{n-1}}m_n^{k_n}} \ . </math>
